records.Entity / project type: integrated miner-operator and ASIC hardware manufacturer
records.Concise description: Bitdeer is an integrated mining technology company that operates mining infrastructure while designing and selling its own SEALMINER ASIC machine family.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitdeer’s 2026 filings and product announcements show an unusual vertical integration: the company operates/self-mines while also developing SEAL ASIC chips and SEALMINER systems for internal deployment and external sales. MSC consolidates the company and SEALMINER hardware family into one canonical hardware profile rather than creating a separate public-miner stock profile.
Creators / founders: Jihan Wu — founder / chairman of Bitdeer
records.Launch / history: Bitdeer was formed from the Bitmain cloud/mining-services lineage and later developed its own SEALMINER ASIC platform; A4-series hardware was announced for 2026 production.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It illustrates vertical integration across ASIC design, machine sales, data centers, and self-mining without making market capitalization an inclusion criterion.
Important technical or cultural characte: Public-company metrics are not the reason for inclusion
records.Verification basis: Current 2026 Bitdeer product announcements and filings verify active SEALMINER development/production and integrated mining operations.
Research notes / uncertainties: Any hashrate, fleet, efficiency, or capacity figures must be tied to a specific 2026 filing/model/date.
Keep the profile centered on mining technology/infrastructure, not equity-market performance.

records.Concise description: Braiins’ custom Bitcoin ASIC firmware, focused on autotuning, power control, monitoring, and Stratum V2 support on supported miners.
records.Deeper researched summary: Braiins OS is distinct from Braiins Pool: one is firmware running on mining machines, the other is a pool service. Current 2026 releases continue adding hardware support and tuning features. Firmware can alter ASIC voltage/frequency, power targets, thermal behavior, and networking/protocol support, but it cannot change Bitcoin consensus rules.
records.Launch / history: First released as an open-source mining firmware project in 2018; maintained as Braiins OS with active 2026 releases.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is one of the most influential modern custom firmware platforms and demonstrates how software changes machine efficiency/control without changing the underlying ASIC chip or Bitcoin consensus.
Important technical or cultural characte: Stratum V1 and Stratum V2 support on supported configurations
Separate canonical entity from Braiins Pool
records.Verification basis: Current Braiins product and 2026 release materials verify active firmware support.
Research notes / uncertainties: Hardware compatibility and performance gains vary by machine, cooling, power limits, and release; do not publish universal efficiency improvements.

records.Concise description: Luxor Technology’s custom ASIC firmware for supported Bitcoin miners, providing tuning, power controls, monitoring, and fleet integrations.
records.Deeper researched summary: LuxOS is maintained separately from Luxor Mining Pool and can be used as firmware infrastructure across supported ASIC fleets. Current 2026 documentation and changelogs show ongoing releases. Like other firmware, it changes machine operation and pool connectivity rather than Bitcoin consensus.
records.Launch / history: Developed by Luxor during the 2020s; active firmware releases continued through July 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It provides a second major custom-firmware reference and helps distinguish miner control software from pool payout infrastructure.
records.Verification basis: Current Luxor-controlled firmware documentation/changelog verifies active support in 2026.
Research notes / uncertainties: Supported models and tuning results are release-specific and should be checked before public compatibility claims.

records.Concise description: Con Kolivas’s influential open-source Bitcoin mining software that evolved from GPU-era mining into a widely reused FPGA/ASIC miner and driver codebase.
records.Deeper researched summary: CGMiner became foundational software across the transition from GPUs to FPGAs and ASICs and implemented multi-pool operation, Stratum support, numerous device drivers, monitoring APIs, and hardware-control logic. The original GitHub repository was archived by its owner in May 2020, so it is classified HISTORICAL even though descendants, vendor forks, APIs, and concepts continue to influence mining systems.
records.Launch / history: Created in 2011 from the cpuminer lineage; evolved through the FPGA/ASIC transition; original repository archived May 27, 2020.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is one of the most important software lineages in Bitcoin mining hardware control and pool communication.
records.Verification basis: Creator-controlled archived repository verifies authorship, scope, hardware support, and 2020 archival state.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply the original CGMiner repository is still actively maintained because vendor descendants remain in use.
